implementation: Allow same-revision ASCII-to-binary replay of the existing checked IMAGE dictionary graph for selected standard-block LINE/IMAGE documents. Reuse the graph and entity inspectors, require bounded printable ASCII and matching source/decoded text, signed 16-bit integer values and no reserved root names; unsupported captures keep the prior reported-loss fallback. Regenerated IMAGE source objects and removed entries continue to be reported.
validation: New no-unmodeled-record-loss controls failed before the change. Thirteen focused image, dictionary and paper-space tests and eighteen layout tests pass afterward.

A fresh libdxfrw binary import sees the selected LC_REACTOR dictionary, its XRECORD owner and text. Escaped and over-255-byte text, foreign image identity and unsupported child references retain the reported-loss fallback; a subsequent ASCII save succeeds.
Paper-space content fails without replacing the destination and a corrected retry on the same DXFimpl succeeds. Low source handles remap to distinct IMAGEDEFs; the test also verifies reopen.

ezdxf 1.4.5 independently audits four final-head R2000 binary outputs with zero errors and zero fixes. Mixed and empty outputs retain LC_REACTOR owner C and KEEP XRECORD owner 90 with value keep-value. Distinct and low-handle outputs retain two IMAGE-to-IMAGEDEF links and their selected dimensions and pixel sizes.
limits: The admitted sources are locally authored R2000 ASCII with bounded ordinary dictionaries and text-only XRECORDs. Unknown fields, other roots, text/codepage cases, image/reactor source metadata and full graph identity remain unqualified.
This does not establish binary-to-ASCII replay after a later reopen, native rendering, external producer semantics or whole-drawing parity. Generated drawings remain in scratch storage.
